gloss: to be struck by; to be afflicted with (disaster, misfortune, illness)

definitions.gloss: to be struck by; to be afflicted with (a disaster, misfortune, illness, or unwelcome event)
definitions.explanation: The passive form of {見舞|みま}う ("to inquire after, to visit a sick person; to befall"). In its most common modern use, {見舞|みま}われる means to suffer or be hit by something unpleasant — typhoons, earthquakes, accidents, illness, financial troubles. Almost always used with {に} marking the misfortune.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}に{見舞|みま}われた。
examples.english: We were hit by a typhoon.

examples.japanese: その{町|まち}は{大雨|おおあめ}による{洪水|こうずい}に{見舞|みま}われた。
examples.english: The town was struck by flooding from heavy rain.

examples.japanese: {帰国|きこく}の{途中|とちゅう}、{思|おも}わぬトラブルに{見舞|みま}われた。
examples.english: On my way home, I ran into unexpected trouble.

examples.japanese: {地震|じしん}と{津波|つなみ}という{二|ふた}つの{災害|さいがい}に{見舞|みま}われ、{復興|ふっこう}には{長|なが}い{時間|じかん}がかかった。
examples.english: Struck by the dual disasters of an earthquake and tsunami, the recovery took a long time.

notes:
{見舞|みま}われる is the passive form of {見舞|みま}う and is by far the more common form in everyday and journalistic Japanese when describing being hit by misfortune. The pattern is essentially fixed: [victim/place]が[misfortune]に{見舞|みま}われる.

GRAMMATICAL PATTERN:
- ～が～に{見舞|みま}われる: [subject] is struck by [misfortune]
  - {町|まち}が{台風|たいふう}に{見舞|みま}われた: "The town was struck by a typhoon."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {台風|たいふう}に{見舞|みま}われる: to be hit by a typhoon
- {地震|じしん}に{見舞|みま}われる: to be struck by an earthquake
- {病|やまい}に{見舞|みま}われる: to fall ill (literary)
- {不幸|ふこう}に{見舞|みま}われる: to be visited by misfortune
- トラブルに{見舞|みま}われる: to run into trouble
- {不景気|ふけいき}に{見舞|みま}われる: to be hit by an economic downturn
- {寒波|かんぱ}に{見舞|みま}われる: to be hit by a cold snap

SIMILAR / RELATED TERMS:
- {遭|あ}う: to encounter, to meet with (a misfortune); more colloquial. {事故|じこ}に{遭|あ}う ("to be in an accident")
- {襲|おそ}われる: to be attacked, to be assailed; stronger, often used for both attacks and sudden physical sensations ({不安|ふあん}に{襲|おそ}われる "to be overcome with anxiety")
- {被|こうむ}る: to suffer (formal/literary; takes the misfortune as direct object: {被害|ひがい}を{被|こうむ}る)

USAGE NOTES:
- {見舞|みま}う itself originally meant "to inquire after, to visit (a sick person)," and that older sense survives in {お{見舞|みま}い} ("a sympathy visit / get-well gift"). The modern "to befall" sense was extended from there: misfortune "visits" the victim.
- The active form {見舞|みま}う in the "to befall" sense (e.g., {台風|たいふう}が{町|まち}を{見舞|みま}った) is heard mainly in literary or news writing; the passive {見舞|みま}われる is far more common in speech.
- Almost always negative in connotation. To say someone was "visited" by a positive event, use {訪|おとず}れる or {恵|めぐ}まれる instead.

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {見舞|みま}われませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {見舞|みま}われていなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {見舞|みま}われていませんでした
